elements.element: Vendor must expressly defend Customer and its affiliates against covered third-party claims.
elements.evidence: The clause grants the indemnifying party control of the defense but does not impose an affirmative duty on TrueLink to defend.

elements.element: Vendor must indemnify Customer and its affiliates against covered third-party claims and resulting losses.
elements.evidence: Section b requires TrueLink to indemnify and hold Client and its affiliates harmless from claims, expenses, losses, liabilities, and reasonable attorneys' fees.

elements.element: Covered claims must include third-party allegations that the services or deliverables infringe or misappropriate intellectual property rights.
elements.evidence: Section b(ii) expressly covers allegations that the Interface, Hosting Services, Support Services, or other TrueLink materials or deliverables infringe or misappropriate a third party's patent, copyright, trademark, trade secret, or other IP right.

elements.element: Covered claims must include claims arising from Vendor's breach of applicable law.
elements.evidence: Section b(iii) covers any breach by TrueLink of any applicable law, rule, or regulation.

elements.element: Covered claims must include claims arising from a data breach caused by Vendor.
elements.evidence: Section b(iv) covers unauthorized access to or disclosure of Client Content or other Client data caused by TrueLink.

elements.element: Covered claims must include claims arising from Vendor's gross negligence or willful misconduct.
elements.evidence: Section b(v) expressly covers TrueLink's gross negligence or willful misconduct.

elements.element: The indemnity procedure must require prompt notice of a claim.
elements.evidence: The indemnified party must give the indemnifying party prompt written notice of any claim.

elements.element: The indemnity procedure must give the indemnifying party control of the defense.
elements.evidence: The clause states that the indemnifying party shall have control of the defense.

elements.element: The indemnity procedure must give the indemnifying party control of settlement, subject to appropriate protection for the indemnified party.
elements.evidence: The indemnifying party controls settlement, but may not enter a settlement imposing an obligation or admission on the indemnified party without its consent.

elements.element: The indemnity procedure must require reasonable cooperation by the indemnified party.
elements.evidence: The indemnified party must provide reasonable cooperation at the indemnifying party's expense.

elements.element: Customer's indemnity must cover claims arising from Customer-provided content.
elements.evidence: Section a(iii) covers claims arising from Client Content, including content posted by Client or its personnel.

elements.element: Customer's indemnity must cover claims arising from Customer's breach of applicable law.
elements.evidence: Section a(ii) includes claims resulting from Client acts or omissions constituting a violation of state or federal law, rule, or regulation.

elements.element: Customer's indemnity must contain no triggers other than Customer-provided content and Customer's breach of applicable law.
elements.evidence: Section a additionally covers any Client breach of the Agreement, acts causing TrueLink to breach specified third-party agreements, claims relating generally to the Website, and injury or property damage caused by products, services, or information sold, distributed, or transmitted from the Website.

elements.element: Vendor must indemnify Customer against third-party claims alleging that the services or deliverables infringe or misappropriate intellectual property rights.
elements.evidence: Section b(ii) provides an express third-party IP infringement and misappropriation indemnity covering the Interface, Hosting Services, Support Services, and other materials or deliverables.

elements.element: The IP indemnity must exclude infringement caused by Customer modifications.
elements.evidence: No exclusion addresses modifications made by or for Client.

elements.element: The IP indemnity must exclude infringement caused by combinations with items not supplied or authorized by Vendor.
elements.evidence: No combination exclusion appears in the clause.

elements.element: The IP indemnity must exclude infringement resulting from compliance with Customer-provided specifications.
elements.evidence: No Customer-specifications exclusion appears in the clause.

elements.element: The IP remedies must include procurement of the right for Customer to continue using the affected service or deliverable.
elements.evidence: The clause contains no obligation to procure continued usage rights.

elements.element: The IP remedies must include modification of the affected service or deliverable to make it non-infringing.
elements.evidence: The clause contains no modification remedy.

elements.element: The IP remedies must include replacement of the affected service or deliverable with a non-infringing alternative.
elements.evidence: The clause contains no replacement remedy.

elements.element: The IP remedies must include a refund remedy when continued use, modification, or replacement is unavailable.
elements.evidence: The clause contains no refund remedy.

elements.element: Vendor's indemnity liability must be subject to a super-cap equal to three times annual fees.
elements.evidence: No indemnity cap or three-times-annual-fees super-cap appears in the rendered clause.

result.reason: The redline adds most preferred Vendor indemnity triggers and a standard claims procedure, but it does not impose an express duty to defend and leaves Client's indemnity materially broader than the two permitted categories. It also omits every fallback exclusion, infringement remedy, and the 3× annual-fees super-cap. The changes do not negate unrelated commercial terms, but the drafting retains awkward duplication and grants defense control without an affirmative defense obligation.
